name: Asylum -- International Protection (Refugee Status / Subsidiary Protection)

qualifying_event.description: A person with a well-founded fear of persecution or a serious risk of harm may apply for international protection at the border or within Romania, at IGI's Asylum and Integration Directorate (DAI), Border Police offices, police units, or penitentiary structures.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Application registered within 3 working days at IGI-DAI directly, 6 working days elsewhere, or 10 days during a mass-influx situation.

requirements.blocker_text: Meets the well-founded-fear-of-persecution standard for refugee status, or the serious-harm standard for subsidiary protection.
A first-instance decision must be issued within 30 days of the case file's assignment to a case officer.

outcome.duration_length: protection status duration not specified in sources fetched; appeal against a negative first-instance decision must be filed within 10 days, which automatically suspends removal pending the Regional Court's review

sources.title: General Inspectorate for Immigration (IGI), Romanian Ministry of Internal Affairs, Asylum and Integration Directorate (DAI) -- general description of the asylum system: registration, Dublin-procedure determinations, identity documents for protected persons, material/financial assistance, integration support

General Inspectorate for Immigration (IGI) -- description of the asylum procedure: interview, country-of-origin-information cross-reference, written decision, notice delivery; ordinary and accelerated procedure tracks; right to remain and protection against removal during the procedure

Asylum Information Database (AIDA, EU-funded, European Council on Refugees and Exiles) -- Romania short overview: registration deadlines (3/6/10 working days), 30-day first-instance decision timeframe, 10-day appeal window to Regional Court with automatic suspensive effect

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Romania). STATUS: DRAFT -- IGI's own pages (tier-1) describe the procedure's structure but omit concrete timeframes and appeal deadlines, which were sourced instead to AIDA (Asylum Information Database, an EU-funded NGO consortium tracked as tier-2 in this dataset's convention, consistent with prior country builds' use of UNHCR/EU-adjacent intergovernmental sources). work_rights/study_rights set to restricted and family_can_join/family_can_work set to false as conservative defaults -- none of the fetched sources specified when or whether asylum seekers may work while pending, or family-reunification rights specifically for protection holders (as opposed to Romanian citizens or long-stay residents generally, covered in ro_family_reunification.json); disclosed as a gap rather than assumed. Romania's asylum system distinguishes refugee status from subsidiary protection but the fetched sources did not detail differing entitlements between the two -- modeled as a single combined route pending further research. duration_length intentionally does not state a status validity period since none was confirmed in this pass, rather than guessing a figure.
